newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong welcomes Canada visa waiver.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong welcomes Canada visa waiver.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Thursday welcomed a decision by Canada to continue to waive visa requirements for Hong Kong passport holders after China takes the territory back from Britain on July 1.
"I very much welcome the Canadian government's announcement this morning that they will grant visa-free access to holders of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passports," Patten said.
"This is good news for Hong Kong," he said in a statement, adding that he hoped more countries would follow suit.
Hong Kong people currently hold various documents, including limited British overseas passports that give no right of abode in Britain but allow visa-free entry to many countries.
After China resumes sovereignty of Hong Kong on July 1, the new authorities will issue SAR passports to several million eligible residents.
To boost confidence and ease travel, the territory wants as many countries as possible to recognise these documents and grant visa-free access.
Before Canada's move, Britain and Singapore were the only major states to have pledged visa-free entry for SAR passports.
